title: Constant functors and product lifts preserve filtered colimits
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, ordinary categories $\mathcal C,\mathcal A$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets, and an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ (a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$). A category is $\lambda$-filtered if each diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone. Assume $\mathcal C$ has all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits, and let $V:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ preserve them. Colimits mean [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; preservation means that applying $V$ to a colimit cocone gives a colimit cocone. Let $S$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set and $(A_s)_{s\in S}$ a family of objects of $\mathcal A$. The product category $\mathcal A^S$ has objects and morphisms given by $S$-indexed families, with componentwise identities and composition. The constant functor $H:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A^S$, $H(X)=(A_s)_s$ and $H(f)=(\mathrm{id}_{A_s})_s$, and the product lift $K:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A^S$, $K(X)=(VX)_s$ and $K(f)=(Vf)_s$, both preserve small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. This holds also when $S$ is empty, when the product category is terminal. In particular, taking $V=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ gives preservation by the constant and diagonal functors out of any category admitting those colimits.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line per clause: for K, CategoryTheory.pi.coconeOfCoconeEvalIsColimit (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Pi.lean:91-99) applied to the same preserved colimit cocone V(c) in every coordinate gives IsColimit(K(c)); its assembled cocone is definitionally K(c). For H, CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitConstCocone (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Connected.lean:83-90) in the product category gives IsColimit(H(c)), since H(c) is the identity-legged constant cocone. An infinite-cardinal-filtered category is filtered by restriction to finite diagrams; CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.isConnected (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Filtered/Connected.lean:33-35) supplies connectedness. Both declarations allow an empty coordinate set; neither requires all colimits in A.
